note: Research catalogue for the integration dashboard (/data → Integrations). For each operator: the concrete official sources Pingwi could take data from, and how far that investigation has got. This file is PLANNING DATA ONLY — the scrape pipeline never reads it; a source only becomes real by getting a data/sources/registry.json entry. `integrationStatus` here is a fallback: the dashboard derives `integrated` / `needs-maintenance` from the registry and tonight's payload, so it can never claim Pingwi is fetching something it isn't. `lastChecked: null` means nobody has opened the URL and confirmed it since it was written down.

difficultyGuide.easy: GTFS zip over plain HTTP — the generic gtfs-sleeper adapter already handles this shape; a registry entry plus a sleeper allowlist is the whole job.
difficultyGuide.medium: Documented JSON/REST/GraphQL, or a standard XML dialect — needs a new adapter but no reverse engineering.
difficultyGuide.hard: HTML scraping, an undocumented booking backend, or a feed behind registration/contract.

UZ.notes: Biggest single block of Back-on-Track routes on the map. Ukrzaliznytsia publishes no open data and no GTFS; searched data.gov.ua and the UZ site and found only human-readable timetables. The only machine-readable surface is the booking backend behind booking.uz.gov.ua — same category as the ÖBB nightjet.com API we already use, so it is a real option, just an undocumented one.

sources.name: UZ booking backend (undocumented)
sources.notes: Not documented and not licensed as open data. Needs a probe run before committing to it; terms of use must be checked.

sources.name: UZ passenger timetable (HTML)
sources.notes: Official but human-readable only. Fallback if the booking backend is unusable.

CFR.notes: Romania's annual national timetable, valid 12 months from the second Sunday in December. Two ways in, and only one of them works from CI. data.gov.ro publishes the source XML but is NOT reachable from the GitHub Actions runner — the `cfr` entry pointed there for 14 nights and never once succeeded (lastSuccessAt: null, 'fetch failed' after a ~10s connect timeout). The same timetable arrives as GTFS through the Mobility Database (mdb-3236, Transitous' conversion of the S.C. Informatică Feroviară data) on the self-updating latest.zip alias already used for European Sleeper, and that host is reachable. The GTFS is also strictly richer: coordinates on all 1695 stops, real shapes.txt geometry, per-date calendars, and the operator's own IR-N (InterRegio de Noapte) category, which is the night-train allowlist rather than a heuristic over it. The feed stops at the national border, so scripts/adapters/cfr-gtfs.mjs splices Back-on-Track's foreign stretch back on and drops any train whose endpoints then disagree with its row. Flip `trusted` once a night's log on main shows 36 entries matched and 0 dropped.

sources.name: Mobility Database mdb-3236 — Romanian railway operators (GTFS)
sources.notes: What the nightly `cfr` entry reads. latest.zip is the self-updating alias, refreshed on the same cadence as mdb-3107 (European Sleeper). feed_info declares 20251214-20261212, the current annual timetable. Carries all seven Romanian carriers; the allowlist in data/sources/cfr-sleepers.json selects the 36 Back-on-Track row directions. Check it against the live feed with `npm run probe-gtfs -- --verify-allowlists`.

sources.name: data.gov.ro — Mers tren, SNTFC "CFR Calatori" S.A. (upstream XML)
sources.notes: The primary publication, and the upstream of the GTFS above. Recorded as broken for US specifically: unreachable from the GitHub Actions runner (14 consecutive nightly failures) and from a dev sandbox. The adapter that read it directly is deleted — a path nobody can run is not a path — so reviving this would mean restoring scripts/adapters/cfr.mjs and scripts/lib/cfr-mers-tren.mjs from git history.

TCDD.notes: No open data programme and no GTFS found for TCDD Taşımacılık. The e-bilet reservation backend is the only machine-readable surface — the same undocumented-booking-API pattern as Nightjet, so it is workable but needs a probe first.

sources.name: TCDD e-bilet reservation backend (undocumented)
sources.notes: Undocumented. Probe from Actions before writing an adapter (see .github/workflows/probe-oncf.yml for the pattern).

SNCF.notes: Registry entry `sncf` reads the GTFS export nightly; the 'Probe GTFS feed' run confirmed it downloads and parses (698 routes, 39 040 trips, 8 720 stops) and carries all nine of our SNCF routes. Two things shape the integration: the feed has no shapes.txt, so geometry would be a station chain or OSM; and its route names are not addresses — route_long_name is "-" for six of the eleven Intercités de Nuit and files two of the named ones under another corridor — so the allowlist addresses each train as an oriented endpoint pair (data/sources/sncf-sleepers.json). Enrichment is via-only: the live run matched all 18 oriented entries and returned 8–16 stops per train against Back-on-Track's 2–5, but endpoint times disagreed with it by over an hour on four of ten runs and service days came out per-trip, because a date-expanded feed gives each trip its own service_id. Verified by `probe-gtfs --verify-allowlists` on every run of the 'Probe GTFS feed' workflow.

sources.name: SNCF Open Data — theoretical timetables (GTFS)
sources.notes: Also mirrored on the French national access point: https://transport.data.gouv.fr/datasets/horaires-sncf. Probed 2026-09-11: HTTP 200, unzips, tables agency/calendar_dates/feed_info/routes/stop_times/stops/transfers/trips — no shapes.txt and no calendar.txt (calendar_dates only, which serviceDisplay already summarises).

sources.name: SNCF Open Data — theoretical timetables (NeTEx)
sources.notes: Same content as the GTFS export in the European standard format. Only worth it if the GTFS export turns out to be missing something — the one known gap is shapes.txt, so check whether NeTEx carries track geometry before reaching for OSM.

sources.name: SNCF Open Data — Tarifs Intercités
sources.notes: Standard-fare (tarif plein) range, minimum and maximum, per origin–destination and class for day and night Intercités, ODbL, revised with each tariff change (current one from 2 January 2026). Read nightly by the sncf entry's params.openData (scripts/lib/sncf-open-data.mjs) — couchette classes only, since day trains share some pairs. Written blind (the host is unreachable from a dev sandbox); confirm the class labels with the probe.

sources.name: SNCF Open Data — Régularité mensuelle Intercités
sources.notes: AQST monthly counts per selected origin–destination: trains scheduled, run, cancelled and late at the terminus. Per pair, not per train, so it is attributed to a night train only where no daytime Intercités runs the same pair (dayServedStationPairs in gtfs.mjs). Whether the AQST selection includes the night pairs at all is what the probe answers.

MÁV.notes: MÁV has published an official GTFS database since 2016, but it is release-on-request: you submit a form and get a download. That one-off registration step is the only thing between us and a clean feed.

sources.name: MÁV GTFS — download request form
sources.notes: Request access first; the resulting download URL is what the registry entry would point at. Once obtained, this is gtfs-sleeper adapter work.

BDŽ.notes: No official API and no GTFS — searched the BDŽ site and the Bulgarian open data portal. The official timetable exists only as a web search form, so anything here means HTML scraping the same way the cd adapter does for Czech Railways.

sources.name: BDŽ timetable search (HTML)
sources.notes: Official operator timetable, human-readable only. Scraping it is the cd-adapter pattern (scripts/adapters/cd.mjs).

CS.notes: GB rail data is centralised and gated: the industry timetable and Darwin feeds come through the National Rail Data Portal, behind registration and licence acceptance. The Rail Delivery Group is retiring NRDP in early 2026 in favour of the Rail Data Marketplace, so pick the target carefully before building.

sources.name: National Rail Data Portal (Darwin / DTD timetable feeds)
sources.notes: Registration required. Covers every GB operator, so one integration would serve both CS and GWR. NRDP is being retired in early 2026 — check whether to target the Rail Data Marketplace instead.

GWR.notes: Same GB pipeline as Caledonian Sleeper — one National Rail integration would cover both, so treat these two as a single piece of work.

sources.name: National Rail Data Portal (Darwin / DTD timetable feeds)
sources.notes: Shared with CS — see that entry.

VR.notes: Finland is the best-published railway on this list on paper: Fintraffic's Digitraffic serves a daily-regenerated GTFS zip for passenger trains with no key and no registration, plus a documented REST API alongside it. In practice the GTFS URL we hold returns 406 and headers are ruled out as the cause (see the source note), so the URL has to be found before any of this is buildable — hence medium rather than easy.

sources.name: Digitraffic — GTFS, passenger trains
sources.notes: This URL answers HTTP 406 and the cause is NOT headers — do not retry that. Probed 2026-09-12 with a Digitraffic-User identifying the client (their terms ask for one) AND an explicit Accept of application/zip, application/octet-stream, */*: still 406. A server honouring content negotiation cannot refuse */*, so 406 is being used as a generic rejection here and the path itself is the remaining suspect — the same bucket as the VY/ZSSK/HZPP entries, a wrong URL rather than a hostile server. Next step is finding the real GTFS path in digitraffic.fi's railway docs, not sending more headers. Regenerated daily around 05:00 local; once the URL is right this is straight gtfs-sleeper work.

sources.name: Digitraffic railway REST API
sources.notes: Documented alternative if the GTFS export lacks something. Source system is the Finnish Transport Agency's LIIKE.

SJ.notes: Registry entry `trafiklab` reads Trafiklab's GTFS Sweden 3 nightly (TRAFIKLAB_API_KEY scrape secret, keyless Mobility Database mirror mdb-2939 as the fallback). Samtrafiken files night trains as route_type 105 (Sleeper Rail Service) with the train number as route_short_name, so SJ 1/2, 70/71, 91/92 and 93/94 are addressed by number and their service days belong to one train. Checked against the feed of 2026-09-25: SJ 1/2 run Sunday–Friday (Back-on-Track: daily), 91/92 run Stockholm–Umeå and 93/94 Stockholm–Luleå (Back-on-Track had one row, 91/92, labelled Luleå with 93's times), and 93/94 were missing from the map entirely. The EuroNight 345/346 to Berlin (RDC/SJ) is not in the feed.

sources.name: Trafiklab — GTFS Sweden 3 (national feed)
sources.notes: Key passed as ?key=. Bronze tier allows 60 requests per 30 days, so one download a night plus the odd branch refresh fits. 647 MB zip: stop_times.txt is 698 MB and shapes.txt 2.4 GB, so the adapter streams tables out of the zip. Rail shapes are just the stop coordinates (3–17 points per run), so shapes.txt is never read.

sources.name: Mobility Database mirror of GTFS Sweden 3 (mdb-2939)
sources.notes: The same feed, re-hosted daily without a key (checked 2026-09-26: last-modified that morning, feed_version 2026-09-25). The `trafiklab` adapter's fallback. `sweep: false` because the probe sweep would re-download 647 MB to learn what the adapter logs every night.

ST.notes: Snälltåget has no feed of its own; it rides in the Swedish national GTFS, read by the same `trafiklab` registry entry as SJ. The Berlin train IS in the feed, German end included (Berlin Hbf northbound, Berlin Gesundbrunnen southbound, Dresden on Fridays/Sundays), but numbered the other way from Back-on-Track (feed 300 = Berlin→Stockholm) and without Hamburg, which the operator does serve — so the adapter keeps Back-on-Track's stations abroad between two stations both carry. The summer Jämtland train is 24/25 in the feed and 3920/3921 in Back-on-Track; its season runs to 3/4 October, not 27/28 September. Not in the feed: 304/305 (Malmö–Innsbruck, summer) and 3904/3905 (Malmö–Duved, winter).

sources.name: Trafiklab — GTFS Sweden 3 (national feed)
sources.notes: Shared with SJ — see that entry.

VY.notes: Norway is fully centralised on Entur, which aggregates every Norwegian operator and serves an open, documented GraphQL journey planner plus NeTEx/GTFS bulk exports, no key for either. One Entur integration covers VY, SJ Norge and Go-Ahead Nordic — four night routes between them, each of which Back-on-Track describes with 2 to 6 via points. Probed 2026-09-12: the per-codespace GTFS file is the one to build on (see its note); the national aggregate is real but 807 MB of stop_times. Norwegian station names need no alias work, unlike France — all 28 checked against the payload are already there with coordinates, Finse and Dombås and Fauske included.

sources.name: Entur Journey Planner v3 (GraphQL)
sources.notes: Open, no key (an identifying ET-Client-Name header is expected). Transmodel vocabulary, so the adapter maps concepts rather than reading GTFS.

sources.name: Entur open data — national aggregated GTFS
sources.notes: REAL but unusable nightly, confirmed 2026-09-12: downloads and unzips in 35 s, and then it is a whole country of every mode — stop_times.txt 807 MB, shapes.txt 2.6 GB. Past the probe's parse ceiling, and nothing we need is in here that the per-codespace file below does not have. Kept as the documented anchor for the bucket pattern, and as the place to look if a Norwegian operator ever lacks its own codespace file. (The value here until 2026-09-12 was the developer.entur.no documentation page, which the sweep downloaded as HTML every run — a GTFS-format source whose url is a docs page can only ever fail, and three of the four sweep failures were exactly that; see ZSSK and HŽPP.)

sources.name: Entur open data — per-codespace GTFS (Vy)
sources.notes: WORKS and carries what we need: 24 routes, 9 496 trips, 930 stops, agencies Vy and Vy Tåg, and among the routes F1 Oslo S–Charlottenberg–Karlstad and F4 Oslo S–Bergen. F4 is Back-on-Track row 69, the Oslo–Bergen night train. (An earlier note here said this feed held only Vy's Oslo commuter network with no F-line — that was wrong, corrected once the probe started printing a feed's route list.) The night train does not show in the probe's candidate table because Entur writes a past-midnight arrival as 06:23 rather than 30:23, so a duration came out negative; the probe now treats an arrival earlier than its departure as overnight, which is the half of GTFS's two notations it had been missing. Even so the representative trip on F4 is a day train — one night train among thirty day services — so the allowlist entry has to be a NAMED ORIENTED pair, which scans every trip and requires it to cross midnight. shapes.txt is 415.9 MB and is skipped past MAX_SHAPES_BYTES; geometry is the station chain, as SNCF's is.

sources.name: Entur open data — per-codespace GTFS (SJ Nord)
sources.notes: WORKS, confirmed 2026-09-12: 7 routes, 912 trips, 500 stops, agency SJ Nord, and the route list is F6 Dovrebanen, F7 Nordlandsbanen, R60 Rørosbanen, R65 Raumabanen, R70 Trønderbanen, R71 Meråkerbanen, R75 Saltenpendelen. F6 and F7 are Back-on-Track rows 70 (Oslo–Trondheim 405/406) and 71 (Trondheim–Bodø 475/476). Small and cheap: stop_times.txt 0.9 MB. shapes.txt 139 MB is under the ceiling and parses. Like Vy, the night train is one trip inside a line that also runs day services, so the allowlist entries are named oriented pairs.

sources.name: Entur open data — per-codespace GTFS (Go-Ahead Nordic)
sources.notes: WORKS, confirmed 2026-09-12: 3 routes, 1 724 trips, 275 stops, agency Go-Ahead Norge AS — F5 Sørtoget region, L5 Jærbanen, R50 Sørtoget lokal. F5 is Back-on-Track row 65, the Oslo–Stavanger night train (F5 725/726). stop_times.txt 1.0 MB, shapes.txt 108 MB, both fine. The probe shows F5 as a 04:19→12:05 day train because that is the fullest trip on the line; the 22:25 night train is one trip inside it, hence a named oriented allowlist entry.

sources.name: Entur open data — per-codespace GTFS (Vy long-distance)
sources.notes: HTTP 404, and it should never have been tried: it was guessed from a false reading of rb_vyg (that Vy's long-distance was missing from it). F4 Oslo S–Bergen is in rb_vyg, so Vy needs no second codespace and there is nothing here to find. Kept only so the dead end is on the record.

SJN.notes: SJ Nord runs the Trondheim–Bodø night trains under Norwegian franchise, so its data is in Entur, not in SJ's Swedish feed. Covered by the same Entur integration as VY.

sources.name: Entur Journey Planner v3 (GraphQL)
sources.notes: Shared with VY and GA — see the VY entry.

GA.notes: Go-Ahead Nordic's Oslo–Stavanger night train is in Entur like every other Norwegian service. Same integration as VY and SJ Nord.

sources.name: Entur Journey Planner v3 (GraphQL)
sources.notes: Shared with VY and SJN — see the VY entry.

RJ.notes: Two routes in. The Czech infrastructure manager (Správa železnic) publishes the whole national timetable — every operator, RegioJet included — as CZPTT XML through the CIS JŘ portal. RegioJet's own booking API is already used for price probes (scripts/adapters/regiojet-api.mjs), so that surface is known to work.

sources.name: CIS JŘ — national rail timetable (CZPTT XML)
sources.notes: Official and complete for Czech rail — one integration would cover RJ, ČD and Leo Express. CZPTT is a European standard dialect but needs its own parser.

sources.name: RegioJet public booking API
sources.notes: Already called by the weekly price probe, so the endpoint is known good — it just isn't wired to timetables yet.

ZSSK.notes: A Slovak national rail GTFS exists (published via ZSR, covering ZSSK, RegioJet and Leo Express), but I could not confirm the official upstream download URL — only the aggregator page below. Confirm the primary source before building.

sources.name: Slovak rail GTFS (via Transitland aggregator)
sources.notes: Aggregator page — use it to find the official upstream URL, then point the registry entry at that, not at Transitland.

HŽPP.notes: A GTFS feed for HŽPP is known to exist through aggregators, but I could not confirm an official Croatian publication URL. Next step is to find whether it comes from HŽPP itself or from the Croatian national access point.

sources.name: HŽPP GTFS (via Transitland aggregator)
sources.notes: Aggregator page — trace it back to the official publisher before wiring anything up.

RDC.notes: The Alpen-Express is a private German long-distance service. Germany's national DELFI dataset does include long-distance rail, so it is the plausible route in — but it is registration-gated and enormous, and whether a charter operator like RDC appears in it needs checking first.

sources.name: OpenData ÖPNV — DELFI nationwide timetable (GTFS)
sources.notes: Registration required; GTFS/NeTEx refreshed weekly (Mondays). Includes rail long-distance. Check RDC is actually in the feed before committing.

ATC.notes: Romanian carriers each publish their annual timetable on data.gov.ro under the 'mers tren' tag. If ATC has a dataset there, it comes free with the CFR integration — the same parser, a second file.

sources.name: data.gov.ro — 'mers tren' datasets (all Romanian carriers)
sources.notes: Confirm an Astra Trans Carpatic dataset exists under this tag; if not, this operator has no official machine-readable source.

CFM.notes: No open data, no GTFS and no documented API found for Calea Ferată din Moldova. Its two routes are joint services, so the partner operator's feed (UZ or CFR) may end up covering them instead — check that before spending effort here.

ŽS.notes: Srbija Voz — no official machine-readable source found yet. One route, so low value; revisit only if a Balkan feed turns up while working on a neighbour.

ŽPCG.notes: Montenegro Railways — no official machine-readable source found yet. One route, jointly run with ŽS, so the two would sensibly be researched together.

OTE.notes: Optima Tours is a tour operator running charter sleepers, not a railway — there is no timetable feed to integrate. Its single route is realistically a permanent curated entry (data/canonical/routes/) rather than an integration target.

ÖBB.notes: Integrated via the official Nightjet booking API since the nightjet registry entry. Two Back-on-Track rows remain — joint services whose train numbers the Nightjet API does not return.

sources.name: ÖBB Nightjet booking API
sources.notes: Registry id `nightjet`. Also drives the weekly price probe via scripts/adapters/nightjet-offers.mjs.

sources.name: ÖBB open data portal
sources.notes: Not used. Worth checking if the booking API ever stops returning the joint services that still fall back to Back-on-Track.

PKP.notes: Two official sources feed PKP: the Polish GTFS bundle for geometry and the PLK infrastructure manager's API for the authoritative stop lists, including cross-border stations the Polish feed omits.

sources.name: PLK Otwarte Dane Kolejowe API

sources.name: Polish rail GTFS bundle
sources.notes: Registry id `pkp-gtfs`. Community-maintained republication of official Polish data — the polylines come from here.

ČD.notes: Integrated by scraping cd.cz train pages. The CIS JŘ national timetable would be a sturdier replacement and would cover RegioJet and Leo Express in the same pass.

sources.name: cd.cz train detail pages
sources.notes: Registry id `cd`. Operator's own pages, but HTML — brittle by nature.

sources.name: CIS JŘ — national rail timetable (CZPTT XML)
sources.notes: Shared with RJ and LE — a single CZPTT parser would replace the HTML scrape and cover three operators.

LE.notes: Covered today through the Polish GTFS bundle (the Przemyśl–Frankfurt night train). CIS JŘ would be the Czech-side counterpart.

sources.name: Polish rail GTFS bundle
sources.notes: Registry id `pkp-gtfs`; the enrich config lists LE among its agencyIds.

ES.notes: Fully first-party: GTFS from the Mobility Database for geometry and validity, the operator's own timetable page for stops, times and service days.

sources.name: Mobility Database — European Sleeper GTFS (mdb-3107)
sources.notes: Registry id `europeansleeper`. Use the self-updating `latest.zip` alias — the dated URLs are immutable snapshots.

sources.name: European Sleeper timetable page
sources.notes: Laid over the feed by mergePageOverFeed(); the operator's page wins on stops/times/days, GTFS keeps the polyline. Never fatal — a page outage falls back to GTFS.

FS.notes: Integrated via Trenitalia's national GTFS — the operator's NeTEx from the Italian National Access Point (CCISS), converted to GTFS and re-hosted by the Mobility Database — for timetables and track geometry, and lefrecce.it (Trenitalia's booking backend) for fares. Viaggiatreno, the previous source, is a running-status API that only knows a train on a day it runs.

sources.name: Trenitalia national GTFS (Mobility Database mdb-3569)
sources.notes: Registry id `italian`, adapter trenitalia-gtfs. Feed version 2026-10-15 covered 17 Oct 2026 – 10 Jan 2027: 80 ICN routes, 326 trips, every one with a shape. The MDB entry is marked unofficial because the conversion (BusOne) is a third party's; the data is Trenitalia's NAP NeTEx.

sources.name: Viaggiatreno REST API
sources.notes: The previous timetable source. andamentoTreno answers only for a train running that day, so each night's file held 13–24 of the 34 listed numbers, and a train running under a works number (95063 for ICN 1959) was never found. Still the operator's per-train schedule page (operator-booking.json).

CR.notes: The largest automated block on the map (63 routes) — China Railway's official 12306 ticketing system, driven by a curated sleeper allowlist.

sources.name: China Railway 12306 ticketing API
sources.notes: Registry id `chinese`. leftTicket + queryByTrainNo; sticky merge keeps yesterday's trains on a total outage.

SRT.notes: Registry id `srt`. Stops, positions and track from the Ministry of Transport's national GTFS (Namtang); times and per-berth fares from SRT's own booking site D-Ticket, one search per corridor in data/sources/srt-sleepers.json. railway.co.th itself and the ttsview train-tracking site are not usable from GitHub's runners (connect timeout; a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge), and D-Ticket answers some runner addresses and times out on others — the adapter retries once and otherwise rebuilds from last night's file.

sources.name: Namtang national GTFS (Office of Transport and Traffic Policy and Planning)
sources.format: GTFS (daily; mirrored as Mobility Database mdb-1831)
sources.notes: Full stop lists and shapes for most long-distance SRT trains, but their stop times are placeholders (00:01, 00:02 …) and are never read; only the Bangkok-area stubs carry real times. Its fare tables cover the Bangkok commuter lines only.

sources.name: D-Ticket (SRT online booking): getTrip + getTrainCoach
sources.format: JSON behind the booking search (POST, form-encoded, session cookie)
sources.notes: home/Home/getStation (station ids) → booking/booking (sets the search) → booking/booking/getTrip (trains, departure/arrival) → booking/booking/getTrainCoach (coaches, fare per berth). All before login; the site's reCAPTCHA guards login, auto-seat and summary only.

JRW.notes: Sunrise Izumo / Sunrise Seto, Japan's only scheduled sleeper, run jointly by JR West and JR Central and sold by JR West. Parsers written without sight of the live markup (JR's hosts are unreachable from a dev sandbox) — confirm with the probe workflow before trusting the refresh.

sources.name: JR West train timetable pages (JRおでかけネット)

sources.name: JR West Sunrise Seto / Izumo guide page
sources.notes: Berth charge per room type and links to the timetable pages and the official timetable PDF (…/pdf/jikokuhyo.pdf).
